synthesize

/SIN-thuh-size/ · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Synthesize means to combine separate pieces into a new, coherent whole.

For the capstone essay she had to synthesize forty years of court records and oral histories into a single argument.

Example

The review board asked the intern not to summarize the twelve safety reports but to synthesize them: one memo tracing the single failure pattern that ran through all twelve. A summary would have stacked the reports end to end; his synthesis found the shape they made together.

To synthesize is to combine separate pieces so that something new and whole comes out — an argument, a compound, a design. The parts don't just sit side by side afterward; they are worked into a structure none of them contained alone.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

combine: Combine is the broad, everyday word for putting things together, in any way at all. Synthesize is more ambitious: the pieces are worked into a new whole — an argument, a compound — that none of them contained alone.

integrate: Integrate means fitting a part into a whole that already exists. Synthesize builds the whole itself, out of separate pieces that had never stood together before.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

dissect: to take apart piece by piece for examination

fragment: to break a whole into scattered pieces

Where it sits · how much the gathered pieces are transformed into something new

compile → synthesize → fuse

compile vs. synthesize: Compile is weaker than synthesize: compiling gathers the pieces into one place and stops, while synthesizing works them into a new whole that none of the pieces contained alone.

fuse vs. synthesize: Fuse goes further than synthesize — a synthesized whole still shows its working parts, but fused parts have melted together past the point of telling them apart.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — syn-: together, with

Root — thes-: to put, to place

Suffix — -ize: to make, to do; verb-forming

Put it together: Syn- (together) + thes- (to put) + -ize (to make) = to put together. Greek synthesis named a putting-together, and English added -ize to set it in motion: separate pieces placed together so deliberately that a new whole stands up.

Use the root in a new word: hypothesis: By Friday the whiteboard held one circled hypothesis and three coffee rings.

Root Check

Word Choice

academic / constructive — the researcher's verb

Synthesize is the researcher's verb, and rubrics love it because it asks for more than collecting. Summarize shortens one source; compile gathers many; synthesize makes the many say something new together. If nothing new stands at the end, the word hasn't been earned.
